title.narrative: Nutrition Smart CommUNITY: Strengthening Adaptive and Inclusive Food Systems for Improved Nutrition and Climate Resilience in South Asia.

description.narrative: A total of 2,400 people will benefit from targeted capacity-building formats designed to anchor and scale systemic and multisectoral approaches to food security at the local, national and regional levels.50 regional representatives, including decision-makers from South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) institutions and government representatives from the project countries, will receive targeted training on systemic and transformative concepts and will help to transfer supra-regional learning impulses into national strategies and programs.500 food and nutrition systems champions will act as bridge builders between communities, civil society, administrations and market actors at the micro, meso and macro levels. They come from a wide variety of backgrounds – community councils, model farmers, women's networks, local businesses and authorities – and will receive targeted training in systemic thinking, network building, leadership and advocacy. They contribute to embedding local innovations in municipal and regional governance mechanisms.1,000 government employees, advisors and political decision-makers at municipal and district level are key actors in integrating food security into municipal development planning and budgetary processes . Targeted training in cross-sectoral coordination, transparent planning and systemic thinking strengthens their skills to effectively implement multisectoral strategies and improve governance structures.

Overall objective:The food security of vulnerable communities in India, Nepal and Bangladesh is improved through the establishment of inclusive and climate-resilient food systems.Project objective: Government and civil society decision-makers at various levels use community-based and cross-sectoral approaches (local food system approach) to sustainably improve the food security of vulnerable groups.

This phase expands and strengthens the Nutrition Smart CommUNITY (NSC) model by introducing sub-regional structures – Community Collectives – that expand local value webs through Learning Hubs, fostering innovation, knowledge exchange, and economic resilience. Unlike linear value chains, value webs are dynamic, decentralized, and interconnected systems, continuously growing beyond individual communities. They enable circular flows of knowledge, economic exchange, and resources, strengthening food system resilience and self-reliance. For a structural transformation of food systems, the approach will focus on: Cooperation networks and leadership for systemic transformation (micro, meso and macro levels);Adaptive, cross-sectoral governance at the meso level and; Local learning and economic resilience.
